// ----- Index + parent links -------------------------------------------------

const INDEX = new Map();

function register(n, parent = null) {
  n.parent = parent;
  INDEX.set(n.id, n);
  for (const child of n.children) register(child, n);
}
register(PLACES);

// ----- Lookup helpers -------------------------------------------------------

export function findNodeById(id) {
  return INDEX.get(id) || null;
}

// Chain of nodes from the root (Earth) down to and including the node. Used for
// breadcrumbs. Empty array if the id is unknown.
export function pathToNode(id) {
  let n = INDEX.get(id);
  const path = [];
  while (n) {
    path.unshift(n);
    n = n.parent;
  }
  return path;
}

// Fallback used only when reverse geocoding is unavailable: given a [lng, lat]
// find the deepest curated node whose bbox contains the point.
export function resolveByCoords(lng, lat, n = PLACES, trail = []) {
  const nextTrail = [...trail, n];
  for (const child of n.children) {
    if (bboxContains(child.bbox, lng, lat)) {
      return resolveByCoords(lng, lat, child, nextTrail);
    }
  }
  return nextTrail;
}

function bboxContains(bbox, lng, lat) {
  if (!bbox) return false;
  const [w, s, e, n] = bbox;
  return lng >= w && lng <= e && lat >= s && lat <= n;
}

// Every race that applies to a node: its own plus those inherited from every
// ancestor (state governor applies to each city in the state, etc.).
export function racesForNode(id) {
  const out = [];
  for (const n of pathToNode(id)) {
    for (const race of n.races) {
      out.push({ ...race, scopeName: n.name, scopeLevel: n.level });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

// Upcoming events that apply to a node (own + inherited), soonest first.
export function eventsForNode(id, now = new Date()) {
  const out = [];
  for (const n of pathToNode(id)) {
    for (const evt of n.events) {
      const endsAt = evt.end
        ? new Date(evt.end)
        : new Date(new Date(evt.start).getTime() + 3 * 3600 * 1000);
      if (endsAt < now) continue; // already over
      out.push({ ...evt, scopeName: n.name, scopeLevel: n.level });
    }
  }
  out.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start) - new Date(b.start));
  return out;
}

// For the dropdowns: given the current path and a level, return the choices
// available at that level and which one (if any) is currently selected.
export function optionsForLevel(path, levelKey) {
  const idx = LEVEL_INDEX[levelKey];
  let parent = PLACES;
  for (const n of path) {
    if (LEVEL_INDEX[n.level] < idx) parent = n;
  }
  // Single-country build: the State menu always lists U.S. states, even from
  // the whole-world view, so people can skip straight to their state.
  if (levelKey === "state" && parent === PLACES) parent = usa;
  const options = parent.children
    .filter((c) => c.level === levelKey)
    .sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
  const selected = path.find((n) => n.level === levelKey) || null;
  return { parent, options, selected };
}

// ----- Dynamic nodes (search results) --------------------------------------

// Lowercase, strip accents and generic suffixes so "Fort Bend County",
// "Fort Bend" and "fort bend" all compare equal.
export function normalizeName(str) {
  return String(str || "")
    .normalize("NFD")
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, "")
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/\b(county|parish|borough|city of|town of|municipality of)\b/g, " ")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, " ")
    .trim();
}

function nameMatches(n, normalized) {
  if (normalizeName(n.name) === normalized) return true;
  return (n.aliases || []).some((a) => normalizeName(a) === normalized);
}

function findChild(parent, name, level, code) {
  const target = normalizeName(name);
  return (
    parent.children.find(
      (c) =>
        c.level === level &&
        ((code && c.code && c.code.toUpperCase() === code.toUpperCase()) ||
          nameMatches(c, target))
    ) || null
  );
}

// Search the whole subtree (used when a result skips the county level but we
// already have that city filed under a county).
function findInSubtree(root, name, level) {
  const target = normalizeName(name);
  const stack = [...root.children];
  while (stack.length) {
    const n = stack.pop();
    if (n.level === level && nameMatches(n, target)) return n;
    stack.push(...n.children);
  }
  return null;
}

function slugify(str) {
  return normalizeName(str).replace(/ /g, "-") || "unknown";
}

function addDynamicChild(parent, fields) {
  const child = node({
    id: `${parent.id}/${slugify(fields.name)}`,
    dynamic: true,
    ...fields,
  });
  child.parent = parent;
  parent.children.push(child);
  INDEX.set(child.id, child);
  return child;
}

// Show "Fort Bend County" rather than "Fort Bend" for U.S. counties.
function countyDisplayName(name, countryCode) {
  if (countryCode === "US" && !/\b(county|parish|borough|census area)\b/i.test(name)) {
    return `${name} County`;
  }
  return name;
}

/**
 * Turn a geocoder result into a path of place nodes, creating any county /
 * city / district nodes that don't exist yet. Returns the path from Earth down
 * to the deepest place we could identify (always at least [Earth]).
 *
 * United States only: results from other countries return just [Earth].
 * All 50 states + DC always exist (data/us-states.js), so only counties,
 * cities and districts are ever created at runtime.
 *
 * @param {object} desc - normalized geocoder result (see js/geocode.js):
 *   { type, name, country, countryCode, state, county, city, lng, lat, extent }
 */
export function ensurePath(desc) {
  const path = [PLACES];
  if (desc.countryCode !== "US") return path;

  const here = [desc.lng, desc.lat];
  const isType = (t) => desc.type === t;
  path.push(usa);

  // State (always pre-built; never created at runtime)
  const stateName = isType("state") ? desc.name : desc.state;
  const state = stateName ? findChild(usa, stateName, "state", null) : null;
  if (!state) return path; // the country itself, or a state we can't match
  path.push(state);
  const afterState = state;

  // County
  const countyRaw = isType("county") ? desc.name : desc.county;
  let county = null;
  if (countyRaw) {
    const countyName = countyDisplayName(countyRaw, desc.countryCode);
    county = findChild(state, countyName, "county", null);
    if (!county) {
      county = addDynamicChild(state, { name: countyName, level: "county", center: here });
    }
    path.push(county);
  }

  // City / town
  const cityName = isType("city") ? desc.name : desc.city;
  let city = null;
  if (cityName) {
    city = county ? findChild(county, cityName, "city", null) : null;
    if (!city && !county) {
      // Result had no county: reuse the city if we already have it somewhere
      // under this state, and fix up the path to its real ancestors.
      const existing = findInSubtree(afterState, cityName, "city");
      if (existing) {
        const full = pathToNode(existing.id);
        path.length = 0;
        path.push(...full);
        city = existing;
      }
    }
    if (!city) {
      city = addDynamicChild(county || afterState, {
        name: cityName,
        level: "city",
        center: here,
      });
      if (!path.includes(city)) path.push(city);
    } else if (!path.includes(city)) {
      path.push(city);
    }
  }

  // District (e.g. a neighbourhood), only when it differs from the city above.
  if (isType("district") && city && normalizeName(desc.name) !== normalizeName(city.name)) {
    let district = findChild(city, desc.name, "district", null);
    if (!district) {
      district = addDynamicChild(city, { name: desc.name, level: "district", center: here });
    }
    path.push(district);
  }

  // Give the node we ended on the exact point/extent from the search so the
  // camera lands precisely (only for nodes made from search, never curated).
  const target = path[path.length - 1];
  if (target.dynamic) {
    target.center = here;
    if (desc.extent && isAdminType(desc.type)) target.extent = desc.extent;
  }
  return path;
}

function isAdminType(type) {
  return ["state", "county", "city", "district"].includes(type);
}

// data/civic.js
// The ONE module the app talks to for political data. Right now it serves the
// sample data in data/places.js. To go live, replace the bodies of these
// functions with real API calls; nothing else in the app has to change.
//
// Suggested real sources
//   Races / candidates : Google Civic Information API, Ballotpedia, Open States,
//                        Vote Smart, state election offices
//   Events / town halls: Town Hall Project, Mobilize, city & county calendars
//                        (CivicPlus / Legistar / Granicus feeds), League of Women
//                        Voters "Vote411"
//   Geocoding          : see js/geocode.js
//
// Every function is async so swapping in fetch() is a drop-in change.

import {
  racesForNode,
  eventsForNode,
  resolveByCoords,
  ensurePath,
  pathToNode,
} from "./places.js";

// Races relevant to a place id (own + inherited from ancestors).
export async function fetchRacesForPlace(placeId) {
  return racesForNode(placeId);
}

// Upcoming political events relevant to a place id (own + inherited), soonest
// first. Each event: { id, title, type, start, end?, venue, virtual,
// description, url?, source, scopeName }.
export async function fetchEventsForPlace(placeId) {
  return eventsForNode(placeId);
}

// Turn a geocoder result (see js/geocode.js) into a path of place nodes from
// Earth down to the most specific place we can identify.
export async function resolvePlaceFromGeocode(desc) {
  return ensurePath(desc);
}

// Offline fallback: match raw GPS coordinates against curated bounding boxes.
export async function resolvePlaceByCoords(lng, lat) {
  return resolveByCoords(lng, lat);
}

// Convenience: breadcrumb path for a place id.
export async function fetchPathForPlace(placeId) {
  return pathToNode(placeId);
}

// js/globe.js // Wraps MapLibre GL in a real 3D globe and exposes a small API for the rest of // the app: render markers for a node's children, fly to a node, and report // clicks back up via callbacks. // // MapLibre v6 is distributed as an ES module only, so it is imported from the // CDN here (pin the version; bump deliberately). No API key is needed: the // basemap is OpenFreeMap's "bright" vector style. // // Why a vector style: it gives crisp labels at every zoom (country, state, city // names) which helps people who are not used to reading maps. import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.15.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; import { levelByKey } from "../data/levels.js"; const STYLE_URL = "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/bright"; // Free country polygons (MapLibre demo tiles). Each feature has ADM0_A3 (ISO // alpha-3 code, e.g. "USA") and NAME. const COUNTRIES_TILEJSON = "https://demotiles.maplibre.org/tiles/tiles.json"; // Countries that have information in the app. Everything else is greyed out. const ACTIVE_COUNTRIES = ["USA"]; const ACTIVE_COLOR = "#2563eb"; const ACTIVE_OUTLINE = "#1d4ed8"; const INACTIVE_COLOR = "#6b7280"; // Idle motion on the whole-world view: the globe slowly sways left and right // around the U.S. (a sine wave: +/-35 degrees of longitude, ~30 s per cycle). const SWAY_CENTER_LNG = -98; // js/search.js
// Search-as-you-type place picker (an accessible "combobox").
//
// - Type a place ("Medford, MA", "Sugar Land TX", "Paris") and pick a result.
// - Works with mouse, touch and keyboard (Up/Down, Enter, Escape).
// - Requests are debounced and cancelled when superseded, to be kind to the
//   shared public geocoder (see js/geocode.js).

import { searchPlaces } from "./geocode.js";

const DEBOUNCE_MS = 300;

export class SearchBox {
  /**
   * @param {object} refs - { form, input, list, status }
   * @param {object} handlers - { onSelect(descriptor) }
   */
  constructor(refs, handlers = {}) {
    this.refs = refs;
    this.handlers = handlers;
    this.results = [];
    this.activeIndex = -1;
    this._timer = null;
    this._abort = null;
    this._seq = 0;

    const { form, input } = refs;

    input.addEventListener("input", () => this._onInput());
    input.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => this._onKeyDown(e));
    input.addEventListener("focus", () => {
      if (this.results.length) this._open();
    });

    form.addEventListener("submit", (e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      this._submit();
    });

    // Close the list when clicking elsewhere.
    document.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
      if (!form.contains(e.target)) this._close();
    });
  }

  focus() {
    this.refs.input.focus();
  }

  setValue(text) {
    this.refs.input.value = text;
  }

  // ----- Input handling ----------------------------------------------------

  _onInput() {
    const q = this.refs.input.value.trim();
    clearTimeout(this._timer);
    if (this._abort) this._abort.abort();

    if (q.length < 2) {
      this.results = [];
      this._render();
      this._close();
      this._message("");
      return;
    }
    this._message("SearchingΓÇª");
    this._timer = setTimeout(() => this._run(q), DEBOUNCE_MS);
  }

  async _run(q) {
    const seq = ++this._seq;
    this._abort = new AbortController();
    try {
      const results = await searchPlaces(q, this._abort.signal);
      if (seq !== this._seq) return; // a newer search is in flight
      this.results = results;
      this.activeIndex = results.length ? 0 : -1;
      this._render();
      if (results.length) {
        this._open();
        this._message(
          `${results.length} suggestion${results.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}. Use the arrow keys and Enter to choose.`
        );
      } else {
        this._open();
        this._message("");
      }
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.name === "AbortError") return;
      if (seq !== this._seq) return;
      this.results = [];
      this._render(
        "We couldn't reach the search service. Check your connection, or pick a place from the lists instead."
      );
      this._open();
      this._message("Search is unavailable right now.");
    }
  }

  _onKeyDown(e) {
    if (e.key === "ArrowDown") {
      e.preventDefault();
      if (!this.results.length) return;
      this._open();
      this._setActive((this.activeIndex + 1) % this.results.length);
    } else if (e.key === "ArrowUp") {
      e.preventDefault();
      if (!this.results.length) return;
      this._setActive(
        (this.activeIndex - 1 + this.results.length) % this.results.length
      );
    } else if (e.key === "Escape") {
      this._close();
    }
  }

  // Enter / the Search button: pick the highlighted suggestion, or search now.
  async _submit() {
    clearTimeout(this._timer);
    const q = this.refs.input.value.trim();
    if (q.length < 2) {
      this._message("Type a city, county, state or country to search.");
      return;
    }
    if (this.results.length && this.activeIndex >= 0) {
      this._choose(this.results[this.activeIndex]);
      return;
    }
    // Nothing loaded yet (user typed fast and pressed Enter): fetch, then pick.
    this._message("SearchingΓÇª");
    try {
      const results = await searchPlaces(q);
      if (results.length) {
        this._choose(results[0]);
      } else {
        this.results = [];
        this._render();
        this._open();
      }
    } catch {
      this._render("We couldn't reach the search service. Try again in a moment.");
      this._open();
    }
  }

  _choose(desc) {
    this.refs.input.value = desc.label;
    this.results = [];
    this._render();
    this._close();
    this._message("");
    this.handlers.onSelect?.(desc);
  }

  // ----- Rendering ---------------------------------------------------------

  _render(errorText) {
    const list = this.refs.list;
    list.innerHTML = "";
    if (errorText) {
      list.appendChild(emptyItem(errorText));
      return;
    }
    if (!this.results.length) {
      if (this.refs.input.value.trim().length >= 2) {
        list.appendChild(
          emptyItem(
            "No U.S. places found. Try a city and state, like ΓÇ£Sugar Land, TXΓÇ¥."
          )
        );
      }
      return;
    }
    this.results.forEach((r, i) => {
      const li = document.createElement("li");
      li.id = `search-opt-${i}`;
      li.setAttribute("role", "option");
      li.className = "search-option";
      li.setAttribute("aria-selected", String(i === this.activeIndex));

      const title = document.createElement("span");
      title.className = "search-option-title";
      title.textContent = r.name;

      const sub = document.createElement("span");
      sub.className = "search-option-sub";
      sub.textContent = subtitle(r);

      li.append(title, sub);
      li.addEventListener("mousedown", (e) => e.preventDefault()); // keep input focus
      li.addEventListener("click", () => this._choose(r));
      list.appendChild(li);
    });
  }

  _setActive(i) {
    this.activeIndex = i;
    const opts = this.refs.list.querySelectorAll('[role="option"]');
    opts.forEach((o, idx) =>
      o.setAttribute("aria-selected", String(idx === i))
    );
    const active = opts[i];
    if (active) {
      this.refs.input.setAttribute("aria-activedescendant", active.id);
      active.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" });
    }
  }

  _open() {
    if (!this.refs.list.children.length) return;
    this.refs.list.hidden = false;
    this.refs.input.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
  }

  _close() {
    this.refs.list.hidden = true;
    this.refs.input.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    this.refs.input.removeAttribute("aria-activedescendant");
  }

  // Polite screen-reader announcement (also visible as small helper text).
  _message(text) {
    this.refs.status.textContent = text;
  }
}

function emptyItem(text) {
  const li = document.createElement("li");
  li.className = "search-empty";
  li.textContent = text;
  return li;
}

// "Middlesex County, Massachusetts, United States" for a city result, etc.
function subtitle(r) {
  const parts = [];
  const add = (v) => v && !parts.includes(v) && parts.push(v);
  const kind = {
    city: "City / town",
    county: "County",
    state: "State",
    district: "District",
    locality: "Place",
  }[r.type];
  const county =
    r.county && r.countryCode === "US" && !/county|parish|borough/i.test(r.county)
      ? `${r.county} County`
      : r.county;
  if (r.type !== "city" && r.city && r.city !== r.name) add(r.city);
  if (r.type !== "county") add(county);
  if (r.type !== "state") add(r.state);
  return [kind, parts.join(", ")].filter(Boolean).join(" ┬╖ ");
}

// js/geocode.js
// Place search + reverse geocoding using Photon (https://photon.komoot.io), a
// free, key-less geocoder built on OpenStreetMap data that supports
// search-as-you-type.
//
// PRIVACY: what the user types in the search box, and (only when they press
// "Use my location") their coordinates, are sent to photon.komoot.io. Nothing
// else leaves the browser. If you self-host Photon or switch providers, change
// PHOTON_URL below and adapt `toDescriptor`.
//
// Fair use: the public instance is shared, so keep the debounce in search.js
// and don't hammer it. For production, self-host or use a paid provider.
//
// SCOPE: United States only. Searches are limited to a bounding box around the
// 50 states + DC, and results are also filtered by country code (the box
// overlaps Canada and Mexico). Widen both to support more countries.

const PHOTON_URL = "https://photon.komoot.io";

// minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat: covers the 50 states, including Alaska and Hawaii.
const US_BBOX = "-179.3,18.8,-66.8,71.6";

// Only return real places (not shops, airports, hospitals, ...).
const PLACE_LAYERS = ["city", "county", "state", "district", "locality"];

// Normalized shape the rest of the app uses:
//   { type, name, country, countryCode, state, county, city, lng, lat, extent, label }
function toDescriptor(feature) {
  const p = feature.properties || {};
  const [lng, lat] = feature.geometry.coordinates;
  // Photon's extent is [minLon, maxLat, maxLon, minLat]; convert to
  // [west, south, east, north].
  const extent = Array.isArray(p.extent)
    ? [p.extent[0], p.extent[3], p.extent[2], p.extent[1]]
    : null;
  const desc = {
    type: p.type || "locality",
    name: p.name || "",
    country: p.country || "",
    countryCode: (p.countrycode || "").toUpperCase(),
    state: p.state || "",
    county: p.county || "",
    city: p.city || "",
    lng,
    lat,
    extent,
  };
  desc.label = describe(desc);
  return desc;
}

// Human-friendly label such as "Medford, Middlesex County, Massachusetts, United States".
export function describe(d) {
  const county =
    d.county && d.countryCode === "US" && !/county|parish|borough/i.test(d.county)
      ? `${d.county} County`
      : d.county;
  const parts = [];
  const add = (v) => {
    if (v && !parts.includes(v)) parts.push(v);
  };
  add(d.name);
  if (d.type !== "city" || !d.county) add(d.city);
  if (d.type !== "county") add(county);
  if (d.type !== "state") add(d.state);
  // Everything is in the U.S., so only name the country when it isn't.
  if (d.countryCode !== "US" && d.type !== "country") add(d.country);
  return parts.join(", ");
}

function buildUrl(path, params) {
  const url = new URL(path, PHOTON_URL);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (Array.isArray(v)) v.forEach((item) => url.searchParams.append(k, item));
    else url.searchParams.set(k, v);
  }
  return url.toString();
}

/**
 * Search for places matching free text, e.g. "Sugar Land, TX".
 * @param {string} query
 * @param {AbortSignal} [signal]
 * @returns {Promise<object[]>} descriptors, best match first
 */
export async function searchPlaces(query, signal) {
  const q = query.trim();
  if (q.length < 2) return [];
  const res = await fetch(
    buildUrl("/api/", {
      q,
      limit: 15, // fetch extra: some results are dropped by the U.S. filter
      lang: "en",
      bbox: US_BBOX,
      layer: PLACE_LAYERS,
    }),
    { signal }
  );
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Search failed (${res.status})`);
  const data = await res.json();

  const seen = new Set();
  const results = [];
  for (const f of data.features || []) {
    const d = toDescriptor(f);
    if (!d.name || d.countryCode !== "US") continue;
    const key = d.label.toLowerCase();
    if (seen.has(key)) continue; // Photon sometimes returns near-duplicates
    seen.add(key);
    results.push(d);
    if (results.length >= 6) break;
  }
  return results;
}

/**
 * Find the place at a coordinate (used by "Use my location").
 * @returns {Promise<object|null>}
 */
export async function reversePlace(lng, lat, signal) {
  const res = await fetch(
    buildUrl("/reverse", { lon: lng, lat, lang: "en", limit: 1 }),
    { signal }
  );
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Reverse lookup failed (${res.status})`);
  const data = await res.json();
  const feature = (data.features || [])[0];
  return feature ? toDescriptor(feature) : null;
}

// data/events.js
// Factory helpers for civic events (town halls, meetings, debates, voter
// registration drives, election days, ...).
//
// Event shape:
//   id          - unique-ish id
//   title       - short name
//   type        - key of EVENT_TYPES below
//   start       - ISO 8601 date-time string (local time of the event)
//   end         - optional ISO string
//   venue       - where it happens ("City Hall, Council Chambers")
//   virtual     - true if it can be joined online
//   description - one or two plain-language sentences
//   url         - optional link for details / RSVP
//   source      - "sample" for mock data; real feeds should set their own name
//
// The sample events use dates RELATIVE TO TODAY (see daysFromNow) so a demo
// never shows a stale calendar. Real feeds should return real dates.
// Election Day events use the real general-election date.

export const EVENT_TYPES = {
  townhall: { label: "Town hall", icon: "≡ƒÄñ", color: "#b45309" },
  meeting: { label: "Public meeting", icon: "≡ƒÅ¢∩╕Å", color: "#1d4ed8" },
  debate: { label: "Debate / forum", icon: "≡ƒÆ¼", color: "#7c3aed" },
  voting: { label: "Voting", icon: "≡ƒù│∩╕Å", color: "#be123c" },
  hearing: { label: "Public hearing", icon: "≡ƒôú", color: "#0e7490" },
  community: { label: "Community", icon: "≡ƒñ¥", color: "#15803d" },
};

let _seq = 0;
const uid = () => `evt-${++_seq}`;

// ISO string for N days from today at the given local hour/minute.
export function daysFromNow(days, hour = 18, minute = 30) {
  const d = new Date();
  d.setDate(d.getDate() + days);
  d.setHours(hour, minute, 0, 0);
  return toLocalIso(d);
}

// Build an ISO-like local string without converting to UTC.
export function toLocalIso(d) {
  const p = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${p(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${p(d.getDate())}T${p(
    d.getHours()
  )}:${p(d.getMinutes())}:00`;
}

export function makeEvent(fields) {
  return {
    id: uid(),
    type: "meeting",
    virtual: false,
    source: "sample",
    ...fields,
  };
}

export function electionDayEvent(date = "2026-11-03", scopeLabel = "") {
  return makeEvent({
    title: `General Election Day${scopeLabel ? ` (${scopeLabel})` : ""}`,
    type: "voting",
    start: `${date}T07:00:00`,
    end: `${date}T20:00:00`,
    venue: "Your assigned polling place (check your local election office)",
    description:
      "Polls are open on Election Day. Hours vary by state, so confirm yours with your local election office.",
  });
}

// data/levels.js
// The administrative hierarchy the globe drills through.
// The order here drives breadcrumb depth, zoom behavior, and "move up / down" logic.
//
// Each level has:
//   key    - stable identifier used in code
//   label  - plain-language name shown in the UI
//   noun   - lowercase noun used in sentences ("Choose a state or regionΓÇª")
//   zoom   - fallback MapLibre zoom when the camera lands on this level
//            (nodes with a `bbox` are framed to fit instead; see js/globe.js)
//
// SCOPE: the app is United States only for now, so the tree is
//   World -> United States -> State -> County -> City -> District.
// To support other countries later, add a "continent" level between globe and
// country here, add continent nodes in data/places.js, and widen the filters in
// js/geocode.js. Teams can also insert levels (e.g. "ward" below city) without
// touching the map or UI code.

export const LEVELS = [
  { key: "globe", label: "World", noun: "world", zoom: 1.5 },
  { key: "country", label: "Country", noun: "country", zoom: 3.4 },
  { key: "state", label: "State / Region", noun: "state or region", zoom: 6 },
  { key: "county", label: "County", noun: "county", zoom: 8.5 },
  { key: "city", label: "City / Town", noun: "city or town", zoom: 10.5 },
  { key: "district", label: "District", noun: "district", zoom: 12 },
];

// Fast lookups by key and by index.
export const LEVEL_INDEX = Object.fromEntries(
  LEVELS.map((lvl, i) => [lvl.key, i])
);

export function levelByKey(key) {
  const i = LEVEL_INDEX[key];
  return i === undefined ? null : LEVELS[i];
}

export function nextLevelKey(key) {
  const i = LEVEL_INDEX[key];
  if (i === undefined || i >= LEVELS.length - 1) return null;
  return LEVELS[i + 1].key;
}

export function prevLevelKey(key) {
  const i = LEVEL_INDEX[key];
  if (i === undefined || i <= 0) return null;
  return LEVELS[i - 1].key;
}

// js/geolocation.js
// Thin promise wrapper around the browser Geolocation API.

export function getCurrentPosition(options = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    if (!("geolocation" in navigator)) {
      reject(new Error("Geolocation is not supported by this browser."));
      return;
    }
    navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(
      (pos) =>
        resolve({
          lng: pos.coords.longitude,
          lat: pos.coords.latitude,
          accuracy: pos.coords.accuracy,
        }),
      (err) => reject(err),
      { enableHighAccuracy: true, timeout: 10000, maximumAge: 0, ...options }
    );
  });
}

/* =========================================================================
   Mapachusetts
   Design goals: eye-catching globe stage, calm readable information panel,
   large touch targets, strong contrast, and clear focus rings so it is usable
   by people with a wide range of map-reading and tech experience.
   ========================================================================= */

:root {
  --primary: #2563eb;
  --primary-dark: #1d4ed8;
  --accent: #c2410c;
  --accent-dark: #9a3412;
  --ink: #0f172a;
  --muted: #475569;
  --line: #e2e8f0;
  --paper: #ffffff;
  --paper-alt: #f8fafc;
  --space-0: #030612;
  --space-1: #070e26;
  --navy: #0b1530;
  --navy-2: #0f1b3d;
  --focus: #fbbf24;
  --radius: 12px;
}

* {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

[hidden] {
  display: none !important;
}

html,
body {
  height: 100%;
}

body {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.5;
  color: var(--ink);
  background: var(--space-0);
  overflow: hidden;
}

:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid var(--focus);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.sr-only {
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0 0 0 0);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.skip-link {
  position: absolute;
  left: 8px;
  top: -60px;
  z-index: 1000;
  background: #fff;
  color: var(--ink);
  padding: 0.6rem 1rem;
  border-radius: 8px;
  font-weight: 700;
}
.skip-link:focus {
  top: 8px;
}

/* ---------- Buttons ---------- */
.btn {
  min-height: 44px;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 10px;
  padding: 0.5rem 1rem;
  font: inherit;
  font-weight: 700;
  cursor: pointer;
  white-space: nowrap;
  transition: background 0.15s, transform 0.1s, box-shadow 0.15s;
}
.btn:active {
  transform: translateY(1px);
}
.btn:disabled {
  opacity: 0.45;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
.btn-accent {
  background: var(--accent);
  color: #fff;
}
.btn-accent:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: var(--accent-dark);
}
.btn-light {
  background: #fff;
  color: var(--ink);
}
.btn-light:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: #e0e7ff;
}
.btn-ghost {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);
  color: #e2e8f0;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25);
}
.btn-ghost:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
}
.btn-soft {
  background: #e0e7ff;
  color: #1e3a8a;
}
.btn-soft:hover {
  background: #c7d2fe;
}

/* ---------- Top bar + search ---------- */
.topbar {
  position: relative;
  z-index: 40;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 1rem;
  padding: 0.65rem 1rem;
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--navy) 0%, #14275a 100%);
  color: #fff;
}

.brand {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  color: #fff;
  text-decoration: none;
  font-weight: 800;
  font-size: 1.25rem;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.brand-mark {
  font-size: 1.6rem;
}

.search {
  position: relative;
  flex: 1;
  max-width: 640px;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}
.search-icon {
  position: absolute;
  left: 14px;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.search-input {
  flex: 1;
  min-width: 0;
  height: 48px;
  padding: 0 1rem 0 2.6rem;
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  border-radius: 12px;
  font: inherit;
  font-size: 1rem;
  color: var(--ink);
  background: #fff;
}
.search-input::placeholder {
  color: #64748b;
}
.search-input:focus {
  border-color: var(--focus);
  outline: none;
}
.search-btn {
  height: 48px;
}

.search-results {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(100% + 6px);
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  z-index: 200;
  max-height: min(60vh, 380px);
  overflow-y: auto;
  list-style: none;
  background: #fff;
  color: var(--ink);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: 0 16px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
  padding: 0.35rem;
}
.search-option {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  padding: 0.6rem 0.8rem;
  border-radius: 8px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.search-option[aria-selected="true"],
.search-option:hover {
  background: #e0e7ff;
}
.search-option-title {
  font-weight: 700;
}
.search-option-sub {
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  color: var(--muted);
}
.search-empty {
  padding: 0.8rem;
  color: var(--muted);
}

/* ---------- Dropdown browser ---------- */
.browsebar {
  position: relative;
  z-index: 30;
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: flex-end;
  gap: 0.6rem 1rem;
  padding: 0.6rem 1rem 0.7rem;
  background: var(--navy-2);
  color: #e2e8f0;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #22346b;
}
.browse-intro {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  min-width: 170px;
  max-width: 220px;
  line-height: 1.25;
}
.browse-tip {
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  color: #a5b4fc;
}
.browse {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  flex: 1;
  gap: 0.6rem;
}
.browse-field {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 2px;
  flex: 1 1 150px;
  max-width: 220px;
  min-width: 140px;
}
.browse-label {
  font-size: 0.72rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  color: #a5b4fc;
}
.browse-select {
  height: 44px;
  padding: 0 0.6rem;
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  border-radius: 10px;
  font: inherit;
  color: var(--ink);
  background: #fff;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.browse-select:disabled {
  background: #1e2a52;
  color: #8ea0d0;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
.browse-actions {
  display: flex;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}

/* ---------- Status banner ---------- */
.status-banner {
  position: fixed;
  top: 150px;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  z-index: 300;
  max-width: min(92vw, 560px);
  padding: 0.7rem 1.2rem;
  border-radius: 14px;
  background: #1e293b;
  color: #fff;
  font-weight: 600;
  text-align: center;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45);
}
.status-banner[data-kind="success"] { background: #166534; }
.status-banner[data-kind="warn"] { background: #92400e; }
.status-banner[data-kind="error"] { background: #991b1b; }

/* ---------- Layout ---------- */
.layout {
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
  display: flex;
}

.map-wrap {
  position: relative;
  flex: 1;
  min-width: 0;
}

/* Starfield + deep-space glow behind the globe (the canvas is transparent
   outside the sphere, so this shows through). */
#map {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  background-color: var(--space-0);
  background-image:
    radial-gradient(1.2px 1.2px at 20px 30px, #fff 60%, transparent 61%),
    radial-gradient(1px 1px at 140px 80px, #dbeafe 60%, transparent 61%),
    radial-gradient(1.6px 1.6px at 260px 190px, #fff 60%, transparent 61%),
    radial-gradient(1px 1px at 80px 250px, #bfdbfe 60%, transparent 61%),
    radial-gradient(1px 1px at 310px 40px, #fff 60%, transparent 61%),
    radial-gradient(1.2px 1.2px at 200px 310px, #e0e7ff 60%, transparent 61%),
    radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 45%, #12276b 0%, var(--space-1) 55%, var(--space-0) 100%);
  background-size: 340px 340px, 340px 340px, 340px 340px, 340px 340px,
    340px 340px, 340px 340px, 100% 100%;
  background-repeat: repeat, repeat, repeat, repeat, repeat, repeat, no-repeat;
}

.breadcrumbs {
  position: absolute;
  top: 12px;
  left: 12px;
  right: 64px;
  z-index: 10;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 0.15rem;
  width: fit-content;
  max-width: calc(100% - 76px);
  padding: 0.25rem 0.4rem;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: rgba(6, 11, 26, 0.78);
  backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
  border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15);
}
.crumb {
  min-height: 36px;
  padding: 0 0.65rem;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: none;
  color: #cbd5e1;
  font: inherit;
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.crumb:hover {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14);
  color: #fff;
}
.crumb-current {
  color: #fff;
  font-weight: 700;
  background: rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.55);
}
.crumb-sep {
  color: #64748b;
}

/* Bottom-left stack: map key above the how-to hint */
.map-overlay-bl {
  position: absolute;
  left: 12px;
  bottom: 14px;
  z-index: 10;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 8px;
  max-width: 300px;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.map-legend,
.map-hint {
  padding: 0.5rem 0.85rem;
  border-radius: 10px;
  background: rgba(6, 11, 26, 0.82);
  color: #e2e8f0;
  font-size: 0.88rem;
}
.map-legend {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 0.3rem;
}
.legend-item {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}
.swatch {
  flex: none;
  width: 16px;
  height: 16px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  border: 2px solid #fff;
}
.swatch-active {
  background: #3b82f6;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #1d4ed8;
}
.swatch-inactive {
  background: #6b7280;
}

.noscript {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 40% 10% auto;
  text-align: center;
  color: #fff;
  font-size: 1.2rem;
}

/* ---------- Map markers ----------
   IMPORTANT: .map-marker is the element MapLibre positions with its own
   transform. Never set position/transform/margin on it, or pins drift off their
   coordinates. All visible styling lives on the inner button, which is sized to
   exactly the dot so the "center" anchor lands the dot on the coordinate. The
   label hangs below it absolutely and does not affect that. */
.map-marker-btn {
  position: relative;
  display: block;
  width: 20px;
  height: 20px;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  background: none;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.map-marker-dense .map-marker-btn {
  width: 14px;
  height: 14px;
}
.map-marker-dot {
  position: relative;
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--primary);
  border: 3px solid #fff;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
  transition: transform 0.15s, background 0.15s;
}
/* soft pulse ring to draw the eye */
.map-marker-dot::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: -3px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  border: 2px solid rgba(96, 165, 250, 0.85);
  animation: pulse 2.4s ease-out infinite;
}
.map-marker-btn:hover .map-marker-dot,
.map-marker-btn:focus-visible .map-marker-dot {
  transform: scale(1.3);
  background: var(--accent);
}
.map-marker-btn:hover,
.map-marker-btn:focus-visible {
  z-index: 5;
}
.map-marker-label {
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(100% + 6px);
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  padding: 3px 10px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: #0b1530;
  color: #fff;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35);
  font-size: 0.82rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  white-space: nowrap;
  pointer-events: none;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
}
.map-marker-dense .map-marker-label {
  padding: 1px 6px;
  font-size: 0.7rem;
}

/* "You are here" pin: orange, not clickable */
.map-marker-current {
  pointer-events: none;
}
.map-marker-current .map-marker-dot {
  background: var(--accent);
}
.map-marker-current .map-marker-dot::after {
  border-color: rgba(251, 146, 60, 0.9);
}
.map-marker-current .map-marker-label {
  background: var(--accent);
  border-color: #fff;
}

@keyframes pulse {
  0% { transform: scale(0.8); opacity: 0.9; }
  100% { transform: scale(2.1); opacity: 0; }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .map-marker-dot::after {
    animation: none;
    display: none;
  }
  html {
    scroll-behavior: auto;
  }
}

/* ---------- Information panel ---------- */
.panel {
  width: 480px;
  max-width: 46vw;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  background: var(--paper);
  border-left: 1px solid var(--line);
}

.panel-header {
  padding: 1.1rem 1.25rem 0.85rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #eef2ff 0%, #fff 100%);
}
.panel-title {
  font-size: 1.6rem;
  line-height: 1.2;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
}
.level-pill {
  display: inline-block;
  margin-top: 0.4rem;
  padding: 0.15rem 0.7rem;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: #dbeafe;
  color: #1e3a8a;
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
}

/* Welcome card */
.welcome {
  flex: 1;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 1.1rem 1.25rem;
}
.lead {
  font-size: 1.1rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}
.steps {
  list-style: none;
  display: grid;
  gap: 0.75rem;
  margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
}
.steps li {
  display: flex;
  gap: 0.75rem;
  align-items: flex-start;
}
.step-num {
  flex: none;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: 28px;
  height: 28px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--primary);
  color: #fff;
  font-weight: 800;
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}
.scope-note {
  margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 0.9rem;
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: #eff6ff;
  border: 1px solid #bfdbfe;
  color: #1e3a8a;
  font-size: 0.94rem;

.quick-title {
  font-weight: 700;
  margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
}
.quick {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}

/* Tabs */
.panel-body {
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}
.tabs {
  display: flex;
  gap: 0.25rem;
  padding: 0.6rem 0.9rem 0;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
  background: var(--paper-alt);
}
.tab {
  display: flex;
  flex: 1 1 auto;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 0.4rem;
  min-height: 48px;
  padding: 0.3rem 0.6rem;
  line-height: 1.2;
  text-align: center;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 10px 10px 0 0;
  background: none;
  color: var(--muted);
  font: inherit;
  font-weight: 700;
  cursor: pointer;
  border-bottom: 3px solid transparent;
}
.tab:hover {

  background: #eef2ff;
}
.tab[aria-selected="true"] {

  background: #fff;
  border-bottom-color: var(--primary);
}
.count {
  min-width: 24px;
  padding: 0 0.4rem;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: #e2e8f0;
  color: var(--ink);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
  text-align: center;
}
.tab[aria-selected="true"] .count {
  background: var(--primary);
  color: #fff;
}
.tab-scroll {
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 1rem 1.1rem 1.25rem;
}

/* Cards */
.group-title {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;

args.text:
# Mapachusetts 🌎

An interactive 3D globe that helps people find the **U.S.** elections, offices,
town halls and public meetings that matter where they live, plus a research
profile for each candidate (cited news summaries, funding, career, issues).

- **Find a place 3 ways:** type it in the search box, pick from the State /
  County / City menus, or press **Use my location**. Or just click the globe.
- **See what applies there:** an *On the ballot* tab and an *Events & town halls*
  tab, including everything that applies from larger areas (a state's governor
  race shows up for every city in that state).
- **Open a candidate:** highlighted candidate names on a race card open that
  candidate's research page at `/candidates/<slug>`.
- **U.S. only for now.** The whole world stays on the globe, but only the U.S. is
  colored in; every other country is greyed out and explains it isn't available
  yet. Search, the menus and geolocation only accept U.S. places.

> **Most races, candidates and events are SAMPLE placeholders**, labeled
> "Sample" in the UI. The Massachusetts governor and U.S. Senate races list the
> real 2026 candidates. Real datasets plug in through `public/data/civic.js`.

## Run it

It's one Next.js app. The globe is a static site in `public/`, served at `/`;
the candidate and news pages are Next.js routes.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
# open http://localhost:3000
```

The globe needs internet (map tiles, MapLibre and the geocoder load from public
CDNs). Geolocation needs a secure context; `localhost` counts, production needs
HTTPS. The candidate pages need Supabase (see [Candidate pages](#candidate-pages-nextjs--supabase)).

## Routes

| URL                    | What it is                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/`                    | The 3D globe (`public/index.html`, served by a rewrite in `next.config.mjs`) |
| `/?place=<id>`         | Globe opened on a place, e.g. `/?place=us-ma` (ids in `public/data/places.js`) |
| `/candidates`          | Candidate search + research profiles                         |
| `/candidates/<slug>`   | One candidate's profile (linked from the globe's race cards) |
| `/news`                | Latest stored headlines                                      |
| `/politicians/<slug>`, `/?candidate=<slug>` | Old links; redirect to `/candidates/<slug>` |

## Where does X go? (start here when adding data)

| I want to add or change...                    | Edit this                                    | How |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --- |
| A real **data source** (API) for races/events | `public/data/civic.js`                       | Replace the body of `fetchRacesForPlace` / `fetchEventsForPlace`. Return objects shaped like `Race` / `Event` in `public/data/types.js`. **The UI needs no changes.** |
| **Races** for a specific place                | `public/data/places.js` → that place's `races: []` | Use a factory from `public/data/races.js` (`makeGovernorRace`, `makeMayorRace`, ...) for samples, or write a `Race` object (see the Massachusetts races). |
| **Link a candidate to their profile**         | the race's `candidates[]` in `public/data/places.js` | Add `slug: "<slug>"`. It must match a `politicians.slug` in Supabase or a profile in `lib/candidate-profiles.ts`. |
| **Events / town halls** for a place           | `public/data/places.js` → that place's `events: []` | Use `makeEvent({...})` from `public/data/events.js`. |
| A new **county or city** with its own data    | `public/data/places.js`                      | Nest a `node({...})` under its parent state/county. Copy Sugar Land (TX) or Medford (MA) as a template. |
| A new **kind of race** (icon, color, group)   | `public/data/races.js` → `CATEGORY_META`     | Add a category; set it on the race's `category`. |
| A new **kind of event**                       | `public/data/events.js` → `EVENT_TYPES`      | Add a type; set it on the event's `type`. |
| The **levels** (e.g. add "ward" under city)   | `public/data/levels.js`                      | Add to `LEVELS`; add matching nodes in `places.js`. |
| **Exact field names / shapes**                | `public/data/types.js`                       | JSDoc reference for `Place`, `Race`, `Event`, `GeocodeResult`. Point prompts at this file. |
| **Geocoder** (search + "Use my location")     | `public/js/geocode.js`                       | Swap `PHOTON_URL`, or self-host Photon. Also holds the U.S.-only filter. |
| **Which countries are active** on the globe   | `public/js/globe.js` → `ACTIVE_COUNTRIES`    | ISO alpha-3 codes (`"USA"`). Also needs places in `places.js` and a wider geocoder filter. |
| **Map colors** (active vs. greyed out)        | `public/js/globe.js` (top) + `public/styles.css` | `ACTIVE_COLOR`, `INACTIVE_COLOR`. |
| **Look and feel** (globe)                     | `public/styles.css`, `public/index.html`     | CSS variables are at the top of `styles.css`. |
| **Look and feel** (candidate/news pages)      | `app/globals.css`, `components/`             | The navbar matches the globe's top bar. |

### How data flows

```
 search box ─┐
 menus      ─┼─► js/navigation.js (current place) ─► js/app.js ─┬─► js/globe.js   (camera, pins, colored regions)
 geolocation ┤                                                    ├─► js/ui.js      (menus, breadcrumbs, cards)
 globe click ┘                                                    └─► data/civic.js (races + events for this place)
                                                                           │
                                                                           └─► data/places.js (sample tree today; real API tomorrow)

 race card name (slug) ─► /candidates/<slug> ─► lib/candidates.ts ─┬─► Supabase (politicians, news summaries)
                                                                   └─► lib/candidate-profiles.ts (curated funding, issues, myths)
```

Every place carries its own `races` and `events`. When you open a place, the app
collects its own **plus those of every ancestor** (`racesForNode` /
`eventsForNode` in `public/data/places.js`), so put data at the **highest level
that applies**: a governor race belongs on the state, a mayor race on the city.

### Anything not curated still works

All 50 states + DC always exist (`public/data/us-states.js`). Counties, cities
and districts that aren't in `places.js` are created the first time someone
searches for them (`ensurePath`), with no races/events of their own. The UI
tells the user "We don't have local details for X yet" and shows what applies
from above.

## Candidate pages (Next.js + Supabase)

Each profile merges two sources by `slug` (see `lib/candidates.ts`):

- **Supabase:** `politicians` (name, office, party, bio, career history) and
  `politician_news_summaries` (AI-written summaries with numbered citations).
- **Curated profiles:** `lib/candidate-profiles.ts`, hand-written photos,
  status, funding, issue, source, and myth data from the candidate-search
  design. A profile without a Supabase row still appears.

Tabs with no data for a candidate show an empty state instead of hiding.

### Database setup

In the Supabase dashboard, open **SQL Editor → New query** and run, in order:

1. [`supabase/schema.sql`](supabase/schema.sql): tables, indexes, Row Level
   Security (public read).
2. [`supabase/news_seed.sql`](supabase/news_seed.sql): the 2026 statewide
   candidates and their cited news summaries (Oct 10–24, 2026).

`news_seed.sql` is generated from `supabase/seed-data/*.json`. After editing
those files, rebuild it with `node supabase/build-news-seed.mjs`, which also
validates the citations.

### Environment variables

Values live in `.env` (gitignored):

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://<your-project>.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<anon public key>
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<service_role secret key>
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<optional; only for npm run summarize>
```

The `service_role` and Anthropic keys are secrets, used server-side only. Never
commit them or ship them to the browser.

### Refreshing the news

- `npm run ingest`: pulls RSS headlines into `articles`.
- `npm run summarize`: fetches article text (kept in memory only), links
  articles to politicians by full name, and writes cited summaries. Needs
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- `npm run news`: both, in order.

Only headlines, links, short snippets, and summaries are stored, never full
article text.

## Files

```
public/              The globe (static; served at "/")
  index.html         Page structure (top bar, menus, globe, info panel)
  styles.css         Globe styling
  js/
    app.js           Entry point: wires everything together (+ ?place= deep links)
    navigation.js    "Where am I?" state: descend / ascend / jump, menu choices
    globe.js         MapLibre 3D globe: pins, camera, active/greyed-out regions
    ui.js            Renders menus, breadcrumbs, race + event cards, messages
    search.js        Search-as-you-type box (accessible combobox)
    geocode.js       Place search + reverse geocoding (Photon), U.S.-only filter
    geolocation.js   Browser location, as a promise
  data/
    civic.js         THE data seam: the only module the app asks for races/events
    places.js        Place tree + races/events + lookup helpers
    races.js         Race factories + category icons/colors
    events.js        Event factories + event-type icons/colors
    levels.js        World > Country > State > County > City > District
    us-states.js     All 50 states + DC (names, centers, zooms)
    types.js         JSDoc reference for every data shape

app/                 Next.js routes: candidates, news, redirects
components/          Candidate research UI (React)
lib/                 Data layer: Supabase queries, curated profiles, news pipeline
supabase/            schema.sql, news_seed.sql, seed-data/
```

## Deploying to Vercel

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In Vercel, import the repo.
3. Add the environment variables above in the Vercel project settings.
4. Deploy.

## Good to know

- **Privacy:** the text typed in the globe's search box and (only when the user
  presses *Use my location*) their coordinates are sent to the public geocoder
  `photon.komoot.io`. The public instance is shared and rate-limited, so
  self-host or use a paid provider for production.
- **Map tech:** MapLibre GL JS 6 (ES module from unpkg, version pinned in
  `public/js/globe.js` and `public/index.html`). Basemap: OpenFreeMap "bright".
  Country shading: MapLibre demo vector tiles. No API keys needed for the map.
- **Dates:** the sample events use dates relative to today so demos never look
  stale. Election Day events use the real date (Nov 3, 2026).
- **Accessibility:** keyboard-friendly search and tabs, visible focus rings,
  44px+ touch targets, screen-reader labels. Full WCAG validation still needs
  testing with assistive technology and an accessibility review.
- **Not covered yet:** U.S. territories (Puerto Rico, Guam, ...) aren't included,
  and there's no automated test suite.

args.text:
# Mapachusetts 🌎

**Find what's on your ballot, then get to know who's running.**

Mapachusetts is a civic information site. An interactive 3D globe shows the
U.S. elections, offices, town halls and public meetings that apply where you
live. Each Massachusetts candidate has a research profile with cited news
summaries, campaign funding, career history and issue positions, in plain
English.

> **Status:** prototype. The Massachusetts governor and U.S. Senate races and
> the candidate news summaries use real 2026 data. Most other races and all
> events on the globe are sample placeholders, labeled **Sample** in the UI.
> See [What's real and what's sample](#whats-real-and-whats-sample).

## Features

### 🌎 Ballot globe (`/`)

- **Interactive 3D globe.** The U.S. is highlighted; other countries are
  greyed out and explain they aren't covered yet. An idle sway keeps the U.S.
  in view.
- **Four ways to find your place:** search-as-you-type, State / County / City
  dropdowns, **Use my location**, or click a pin on the map. Breadcrumbs and
  **Back up** / **Whole world** buttons move you between levels.
- **On the ballot tab.** Races are grouped by type (executive, legislative,
  local, schools, ballot questions). Races are inherited from larger areas, so
  the governor's race shows up for every Massachusetts city.
- **Real Massachusetts races.** The 2026 governor and U.S. Senate cards list
  the actual ballot candidates. Highlighted names open that candidate's
  profile.
- **Events & town halls tab.** Upcoming meetings, hearings, forums and Election
  Day, with date badges, "in 3 days" labels and online options.
- **Works anywhere in the U.S.** Places without curated data are created on the
  fly from search, with a "no local details yet" note and everything that
  applies from the state level.
- **Shareable deep links:** `/?place=us-ma` opens the globe on Massachusetts.

### 👤 Candidate research profiles (`/candidates`)

- **Search and browse** candidates by name, office or party. Each profile has
  its own shareable URL: `/candidates/<slug>`.
- **Profile header:** official photo, party, current-status badge, term info,
  and links to the candidate's races on the map and to OpenSecrets.
- **Six tabs:**

  | Tab | What it shows |
  | --- | --- |
  | In the News | AI-written summary of recent coverage. Every sentence has `[n]` citations that jump to a numbered list of source articles. |
  | Funding | Total raised, top industry, small-donor share, and bar charts of top funding sources, with plain-English explanations. |
  | Career | Current-status card (committees, what the office means), bio, and a career timeline. |
  | Issues | Positions across 11 topics, each with sub-issues, a support meter, and vote records. |
  | Sources | Research sources tagged by media-bias rating and source type, plus the articles cited in the news summary. |
  | Myths & Facts | Widely shared claims, where they came from, and what the record shows, with a link to verify. |

- **"In plain English" and "Why people are searching this"** boxes explain
  each topic for readers who don't follow politics closely.
- **Honest empty states.** If a tab has no data for a candidate, it says so and
  points to official sources (FEC, OpenSecrets, Massachusetts OCPF).

### 📰 News pipeline (`/news` + CLI)

- **`npm run ingest`** pulls political headlines from RSS feeds into Supabase,
  de-duplicated by URL.
- **`npm run summarize`** reads each article, matches it to politicians by full
  name, and asks Claude for a neutral summary per candidate. Citation numbers
  are checked against the real sources before saving.
- **`/news`** lists the stored headlines and links to the original reporting.
- **Copyright-conscious:** only headlines, links, short snippets and summaries
  are stored, never full article text.

### ♿ Accessibility

Keyboard-operable search (ARIA combobox) and tabs (arrow keys), visible focus
rings, 44px+ touch targets, a skip link, screen-reader labels, and reduced
motion support. Full WCAG conformance still needs testing with assistive
technology and an accessibility review.

## Tech stack

| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Web framework | [Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org) (App Router) with React 19. Server components load data; client components handle search, tabs and the menu. |
| Language | TypeScript 5 (strict) for the app; vanilla JavaScript ES modules for the globe, with no build step |
| Map | [MapLibre GL JS 6.15](https://maplibre.org) in globe projection, [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org) "bright" vector basemap, MapLibre demo tiles for country shading |
| Geocoding | [Photon](https://photon.komoot.io) (OpenStreetMap data), filtered to the U.S.; the browser Geolocation API for "Use my location" |
| Database | [Supabase](https://supabase.com) (PostgreSQL) with Row Level Security (public read-only), full-text and `pg_trgm` indexes, via `@supabase/supabase-js` 2 |
| AI | Anthropic Claude through the Messages API for news summaries (model set by `SUMMARY_MODEL`) |
| News ingest | RSS 2.0 feeds (default: Politico Congress); RSS and article HTML parsed without extra libraries |
| Styling | Plain CSS with custom properties; no CSS framework |
| Tooling | Node.js 20.6+ (developed on Node 24), `tsx` for the CLI scripts |
| Hosting | Built for Vercel (app) and Supabase (database) |

The app has four runtime npm dependencies: `next`, `react`, `react-dom` and
`@supabase/supabase-js`. The globe loads MapLibre from a CDN, and none of the
map services need an API key.

### How it fits together

```
Browser
 ├─ /                 Static globe (public/index.html + js/ + data/), served by a rewrite
 │                      └─ candidate name on a race card ──► /candidates/<slug>
 ├─ /candidates/...   Next.js page ─► lib/candidates.ts ─┬─► Supabase: politicians, news summaries
 │                                                       └─► lib/candidate-profiles.ts (curated)
 └─ /news             Next.js page ─► Supabase: articles

CLI: npm run news
 RSS feeds ─────► lib/ingest.ts ────► articles
 article pages ─► lib/summarize.ts ─► Claude ─► politician_news_summaries (+ article_politicians)
```

Profiles merge Supabase data with hand-curated profiles by `slug`. If Supabase
is unreachable, the curated profiles still render.

## What's real and what's sample

| Data | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Massachusetts governor and U.S. Senate races on the globe | Real 2026 ballot candidates ([GBH News voter guide](https://www.wgbh.org/news/politics/2026-10-22/mass-midterm-election-2026-everything-you-need-to-know)) |
| News summaries for Healey, Minogue, Markey and Deaton | Real coverage from Oct 10–24, 2026: 8 cited articles each, 26 unique articles. Written with AI assistance; verify claims with the linked sources. |
| Curated profiles (Warren, Markey) | Hand-written research. Funding figures cite OpenSecrets. Some status details may be out of date. |
| All other races, and every event on the globe | Sample placeholders, labeled **Sample** |

## Getting started

**Prerequisites:** Node.js 20.6+ and a Supabase project.

1. **Install dependencies**

   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

2. **Set up the database.** In the Supabase SQL Editor, run
   [`supabase/schema.sql`](supabase/schema.sql), then
   [`supabase/news_seed.sql`](supabase/news_seed.sql). Both are safe to re-run.

3. **Add environment variables** to `.env` (gitignored):

   ```
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://<your-project>.supabase.co
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<anon public key>
   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<service_role secret key>
   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<optional; only for npm run summarize>
   ```

4. **Run it**

   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

   Open http://localhost:3000. The globe needs internet access for map tiles,
   MapLibre and the geocoder.

### Scripts

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Start the dev server |
| `npm run build` / `npm start` | Production build and server |
| `npm run ingest` | Pull RSS headlines into `articles` |
| `npm run summarize` | Write cited news summaries (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) |
| `npm run news` | `ingest`, then `summarize` |
| `node supabase/build-news-seed.mjs` | Validate `supabase/seed-data/*.json` and rebuild `news_seed.sql` |

### Deploying

Import the repo into Vercel, add the environment variables above in the project
settings, and deploy. Production needs HTTPS for **Use my location**.

## Project structure

```
public/        The globe: index.html, styles.css, js/ (map, search, UI), data/ (places, races, events)
app/           Next.js routes: /candidates, /candidates/[slug], /news, redirects
components/    Candidate research UI (search, profile tabs, citations, navbar)
lib/           Data layer: Supabase queries, curated profiles, RSS ingest, summarizer
supabase/      schema.sql, news_seed.sql, seed-data/ (researched summaries as JSON)
docs/          DEVELOPMENT.md: where to add data, data flow, file-by-file guide
```

## Privacy and security

- The Supabase `service_role` key is only used server-side. The public can read
  but not write any table (Row Level Security).
- Text typed into the globe's search box, and your coordinates only if you press
  **Use my location**, are sent to the public Photon geocoder.
- `npm run summarize` sends article excerpts to Anthropic.

## Known limitations

- Most globe data is sample. Real civic data plugs in through
  `public/data/civic.js` without UI changes.
- Five candidates have profiles. Other ballot candidates (for example Andrea
  James, Shiva Ayyadurai and Joe Tache) are listed without one.
- The summarizer matches politicians by exact full name, so "Sen. Warren" alone
  isn't linked.
- AI summaries can contain mistakes; citations are there so readers can check.
- U.S. territories aren't covered, and there's no automated test suite.

## Contributing

See [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for where each kind of data
lives, how data flows through the globe, and a file-by-file guide.

overview, tech stack and setup, see the [README](../README.md).

## Routes

| URL                    | What it is                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/`                    | The 3D globe (`public/index.html`, served by a rewrite in `next.config.mjs`) |
| `/?place=<id>`         | Globe opened on a place, e.g. `/?place=us-ma` (ids in `public/data/places.js`) |
| `/candidates`          | Candidate search + research profiles                         |
| `/candidates/<slug>`   | One candidate's profile (linked from the globe's race cards) |
| `/news`                | Latest stored headlines                                      |
| `/politicians/<slug>`, `/?candidate=<slug>` | Old links; redirect to `/candidates/<slug>` |

## Where does X go? (start here when adding data)

| I want to add or change...                    | Edit this                                    | How |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --- |
| A real **data source** (API) for races/events | `public/data/civic.js`                       | Replace the body of `fetchRacesForPlace` / `fetchEventsForPlace`. Return objects shaped like `Race` / `Event` in `public/data/types.js`. **The UI needs no changes.** |
| **Races** for a specific place                | `public/data/places.js` → that place's `races: []` | Use a factory from `public/data/races.js` (`makeGovernorRace`, `makeMayorRace`, ...) for samples, or write a `Race` object (see the Massachusetts races). |
| **Link a candidate to their profile**         | the race's `candidates[]` in `public/data/places.js` | Add `slug: "<slug>"`. It must match a `politicians.slug` in Supabase or a profile in `lib/candidate-profiles.ts`. |
| **Events / town halls** for a place           | `public/data/places.js` → that place's `events: []` | Use `makeEvent({...})` from `public/data/events.js`. |
| A new **county or city** with its own data    | `public/data/places.js`                      | Nest a `node({...})` under its parent state/county. Copy Sugar Land (TX) or Medford (MA) as a template. |
| A new **kind of race** (icon, color, group)   | `public/data/races.js` → `CATEGORY_META`     | Add a category; set it on the race's `category`. |
| A new **kind of event**                       | `public/data/events.js` → `EVENT_TYPES`      | Add a type; set it on the event's `type`. |
| The **levels** (e.g. add "ward" under city)   | `public/data/levels.js`                      | Add to `LEVELS`; add matching nodes in `places.js`. |
| **Exact field names / shapes**                | `public/data/types.js`                       | JSDoc reference for `Place`, `Race`, `Event`, `GeocodeResult`. Point prompts at this file. |
| **Geocoder** (search + "Use my location")     | `public/js/geocode.js`                       | Swap `PHOTON_URL`, or self-host Photon. Also holds the U.S.-only filter. |
| **Which countries are active** on the globe   | `public/js/globe.js` → `ACTIVE_COUNTRIES`    | ISO alpha-3 codes (`"USA"`). Also needs places in `places.js` and a wider geocoder filter. |
| **Map colors** (active vs. greyed out)        | `public/js/globe.js` (top) + `public/styles.css` | `ACTIVE_COLOR`, `INACTIVE_COLOR`. |
| A **candidate profile** (funding, issues, myths) | `lib/candidate-profiles.ts`              | Add an entry with the candidate's `slug`. Shapes are in `lib/types.ts` (`CandidateProfile`). |
| A candidate's **news summary**                | `supabase/seed-data/<slug>.json`             | Then run `node supabase/build-news-seed.mjs` and re-run `news_seed.sql`, or use `npm run summarize`. |
| **Look and feel** (globe)                     | `public/styles.css`, `public/index.html`     | CSS variables are at the top of `styles.css`. |
| **Look and feel** (candidate/news pages)      | `app/globals.css`, `components/`             | The navbar matches the globe's top bar. |

## How data flows

```
 search box ─┐
 menus      ─┼─► js/navigation.js (current place) ─► js/app.js ─┬─► js/globe.js   (camera, pins, colored regions)
 geolocation ┤                                                    ├─► js/ui.js      (menus, breadcrumbs, cards)
 globe click ┘                                                    └─► data/civic.js (races + events for this place)
                                                                           │
                                                                           └─► data/places.js (sample tree today; real API tomorrow)

 race card name (slug) ─► /candidates/<slug> ─► lib/candidates.ts ─┬─► Supabase (politicians, news summaries)
                                                                   └─► lib/candidate-profiles.ts (curated funding, issues, myths)
```

Every place carries its own `races` and `events`. When you open a place, the app
collects its own **plus those of every ancestor** (`racesForNode` /
`eventsForNode` in `public/data/places.js`), so put data at the **highest level
that applies**: a governor race belongs on the state, a mayor race on the city.

### Anything not curated still works

All 50 states + DC always exist (`public/data/us-states.js`). Counties, cities
and districts that aren't in `places.js` are created the first time someone
searches for them (`ensurePath`), with no races/events of their own. The UI
tells the user "We don't have local details for X yet" and shows what applies
from above.

## Candidate pages

Each profile merges two sources by `slug` (`lib/candidates.ts`):

- **Supabase:** `politicians` (name, office, party, bio, career history) and
  `politician_news_summaries` (summaries with numbered citations).
- **Curated profiles:** `lib/candidate-profiles.ts`: photos, status, funding,
  issue, source, and myth data from the candidate-search design. A profile
  without a Supabase row still appears.

Supabase career entries are sorted newest first, and a curated entry with the
same years adds its organization and description. Tabs with no data show an
empty state instead of hiding.

### Seed data

`supabase/news_seed.sql` is generated from `supabase/seed-data/*.json`. After
editing those files, rebuild it:

```bash
node supabase/build-news-seed.mjs
```

The script checks each file before writing SQL: citations numbered 1..n, every
`[n]` resolves to a source, every source is cited, https URLs, and dates inside
the research window.

### Refreshing the news

- `npm run ingest`: pulls RSS headlines into `articles` (feeds are listed in
  `FEED_URLS` in `lib/ingest.ts`).
- `npm run summarize`: fetches article text (kept in memory only), links
  articles to politicians by full name, and writes cited summaries. Needs
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; set `SUMMARY_MODEL` to change the model.
- `npm run news`: both, in order.

## Files

```
public/              The globe (static; served at "/")
  index.html         Page structure (top bar, menus, globe, info panel)
  styles.css         Globe styling
  js/
    app.js           Entry point: wires everything together (+ ?place= deep links)
    navigation.js    "Where am I?" state: descend / ascend / jump, menu choices
    globe.js         MapLibre 3D globe: pins, camera, active/greyed-out regions
    ui.js            Renders menus, breadcrumbs, race + event cards, messages
    search.js        Search-as-you-type box (accessible combobox)
    geocode.js       Place search + reverse geocoding (Photon), U.S.-only filter
    geolocation.js   Browser location, as a promise
  data/
    civic.js         THE data seam: the only module the app asks for races/events
    places.js        Place tree + races/events + lookup helpers
    races.js         Race factories + category icons/colors
    events.js        Event factories + event-type icons/colors
    levels.js        World > Country > State > County > City > District
    us-states.js     All 50 states + DC (names, centers, zooms)

app/
  candidates/        /candidates and /candidates/[slug]

  politicians/       Redirects old /politicians/[slug] links
  layout.tsx         Navbar + footer for the Next.js pages
  globals.css        Styles for the Next.js pages

components/
  CandidateResearch.tsx   Search, profile header and the six tabs
  CitedText.tsx           Turns [n] markers into citation links
  Navbar.tsx              Top bar for the Next.js pages
  ResearchSection.tsx     Shared "Candidate Research" section

lib/
  candidates.ts           Merges Supabase rows with curated profiles
  candidate-profiles.ts   Curated profiles (funding, issues, sources, myths)
  politicians.ts, articles.ts   Supabase queries

  types.ts                Shared TypeScript types

supabase/

```

## Good to know

- **Map tech:** MapLibre GL JS 6 is an ES module from unpkg, version pinned in
  `public/js/globe.js` and `public/index.html`. Basemap: OpenFreeMap "bright".
  Country shading: MapLibre demo vector tiles.
- **Links between the two halves:** the globe is a static page, so links from
  Next.js pages to `/` are plain `<a>` tags (full page load), not `<Link>`.
- **Dates:** the sample events use dates relative to today so demos never look
  stale. Election Day events use the real date (Nov 3, 2026).
- **Geocoder fair use:** the public Photon instance is shared and rate-limited.
  Keep the search debounce, and self-host or use a paid provider for production.
